author: bank_narrative
scope: Complete independent reading of all 17 dated scopes, 68 labels and 68 explanations against the accepted Russian version, followed by complete re-reading after the author corrected the findings below.
checks: Chinese distinguishes armoured and protected cruisers, guns and their mounts, shields and turrets, boilers and funnels, shafts and propellers.
Photographic dates and uncertainty, schematic coordinates and invisible internal armour remain explicit.
Diana's 8-to-6 gun change preserves both calendars and the retrospective report wording; Diana and Pallada do not gain an unsupported boiler count.
Pobeda does not acquire the removed stronger-gun comparison, and Petropavlovsk does not acquire an unsupported claim of underwater armour protection.
Machine comparison confirms all 68 IDs, positions, weapon links, source IDs and photographic URLs remain identical to accepted Russian data.
resolvedFindings: Generic mast labels changed from 桅杆与桅盘 to 桅杆与平台, avoiding an implication that all slender masts had fighting tops.
Varyag's two references to Jane now identify Fred Jane and his 1904 publication explicitly.
Yashima's secondary-gun protection comparison no longer uses 同一炮组, which could imply different protection within a single gun crew.
